title: Firewall Rules
description: Merge overlapping blocked IP ranges to find the lowest allowed address and count all allowed IPs in the 32-bit space.
writeup:
## Approach

This is an **interval merging** problem. Sort the blocked ranges by their start address, then sweep through: if the next range overlaps or is adjacent to the current merged block (start ≤ current end + 1), extend the block; otherwise, start a new one. A single pass produces a sorted list of non-overlapping, non-adjacent merged blocks.

The `+ 1` in the adjacency check is important: ranges `0-5` and `6-9` are adjacent (no gap), so they must merge into `0-9`.

## Part 1

After merging, the lowest allowed IP is simply one past the end of the first merged block — the first gap in the number line.

## Part 2

Sum the sizes of all gaps between consecutive merged blocks, plus any gap between the last block and `4,294,967,295`. Each gap `[prev_end+1, next_start-1]` contributes `next_start - prev_end - 1` allowed IPs.
